CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who presents with right elbow pain that began approximately one week ago while playing lacrosse with his children. He reports that he was throwing a ball when the pain started suddenly. He denies falling but notes that his 13-year-old son was playing roughly and checked him multiple times with a lacrosse stick, which may have resulted in direct trauma to the elbow. The pain is sharp in character and radiates down the forearm. It is elicited with any movement of the elbow. He has taken ibuprofen for a couple of days with some relief. He reports the pain is localized to the tip of the elbow.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies chest pain, abdominal pain, or shortness of breath. Lungs are clear bilaterally. Heart exam notable for known grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur, previously documented.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Hypertension
2. Diabetes mellitus type 2
3. Systolic ejection murmur (grade 2 out of 6)

MEDICATIONS
1. Lisinopril 20 mg daily
2. Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is an active father of two children, ages 13 and 10. He plays recreational lacrosse with his children. The patient and his family follow a Mediterranean diet with low salt intake.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure 150/90 mmHg (elevated).
General: No acute distress.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur noted (known finding).
Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: Right elbow exam reveals tenderness to palpation over the olecranon area of the posterior elbow. Mild pain with flexion and extension. Normal range of motion. Mild swelling and bruising noted.

RESULTS
Right elbow X-ray: No fracture, no bony abnormality. Normal study.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right elbow contusion: Secondary to blunt trauma from lacrosse stick. Patient to take ibuprofen 800 mg twice daily. Ice elbow three times daily for 20 minutes per session. Restrict lacrosse activity for the next couple of weeks to allow healing.
2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Blood pressure elevation today likely related to white coat syndrome. Continue low-salt Mediterranean diet. Recheck blood pressure at follow-up.
3. Diabetes mellitus type 2: Continue metformin 500 mg daily. Obtain hemoglobin A1c to assess glycemic control and determine if dose adjustment needed in the future. Blood glucose readings have been in good range (80-100 mg/dL).
4. Follow-up: Patient to return for follow-up visit. Nurse to provide prescriptions prior to discharge.
